exposure: Elevated markers of coagulopathy (INR > 1.2, fibrinogen level < 234)
Clinically meaningful decrease in fibrinogen level (<150)
cohort: The study included consecutive term and late-preterm neonates who underwent brain MR imaging at a single institution between January 2011 and August 2018.
finding: The study found that intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 9% of term/late-preterm neonates undergoing brain MR imaging, with intraventricular and subdural hemorrhages being the most common types and a high prevalence of venous congestion or thromboses accompanying the hemorrhages.
mod_finding: Among neonates with intracranial hemorrhage, 32% were delivered via cesarean section and 8% via instrumented delivery.
cross-section timing: During the neonatal period, based on MR imaging data collected from January 2011 to August 2018.
